prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1419; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the claimant reported a low-speed collision in a parking lot while backing out of a space. The claimant is unrepresented and has provided a contact number for follow-up.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of the impact and describes the collision as reported. Confirmed that the driver is listed on the policy and that coverage was in force on the date of loss.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant, who described the same sequence of events as in the initial call. The account of how the vehicle moved and where the impact occurred has not changed.

Entry 4: Obtained statements from two witnesses who saw the vehicles make contact in the lot. Both confirmed the accident happened as the claimant described it.

Entry 5: Received photographs from the scene and from the body shop. The damage to the rear bumper and tailgate lines up with the impact described and with the other driver's account.

Entry 6: Contacted the other driver, who confirmed the collision occurred as reported and did not dispute the sequence of events.

Entry 7: Checked the vehicle history and prior repair records. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 8: Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness following the collision and was seen at urgent care the same day. The kind and force of the impact fit the reported symptoms well.

Entry 9: Medical records show the claimant was treated for neck complaints within the past two years. That earlier condition is adding to the current symptoms, so the prior history has been noted for the evaluation.

Entry 10: Treatment followed a usual course of care, including physical therapy and medication. Recent notes show steady improvement, and the frequency of visits has tapered as expected.

Entry 11: Reviewed the current treatment plan with the claimant, who confirmed the same account of the accident and her symptoms in each contact so far. No inconsistencies have been found in the file.

Entry 12: Based on the records, witness statements, photos and vehicle damage, the claim is progressing normally. Remaining items are the final treatment summary and the bills for review.
